proof.title: Exact second-order constructions with repeated Majorana roots
proof.summary: Six cyclic algebraic states and one sparse state establish second-order anticoherence while preserving their stated full multiplicity partitions.
proof.bodyHtml:
All nonzero Dicke coefficients are separated by at least three indices. Consequently the off-diagonal entries of the two-qubit reduced state vanish. The two exact moment identities above then make every diagonal entry equal to one third.

The cyclic family uses P(z)=z^a(z^3−u)^m(z^3−ku), with m equal to two or three and u positive. A univariate integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval define k; a rational function fixes x=u². The constructor verifies that x is strictly positive and that both original moment equations have zero remainder modulo the defining polynomial. Since k is neither zero nor one, the cubic factors have distinct nonzero roots and are coprime. Their multiplicities, together with the projective poles, therefore give the full partition exactly.

The additional eleven-qubit sparse state has two double poles. Its remaining factor A+Bz³+Cz⁷ is squarefree: a repeated root would require (−3B/7C)³=(−7A/4B)⁴, whose two sides have opposite signs. Exact existence does not by itself prove that order two is the largest possible order for a partition.
